newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: No renegotiation of EMU stability pact - Kok.
newsitem.headline: No renegotiation of EMU stability pact - Kok.

text.p: European Finance Ministers, meeting in Luxembourg on Sunday, will not renegotiate the EMU stability pact, Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said on Friday.
"There will be no renegotiation of the stability pact, but there is scope to discuss strengthening employment policy," he told a news conference after the weekly Dutch cabinet meeting.
"I sense the whole of Europe wants to improve employment policy," Kok added.

The left's victory in the French elections has cast uncertainty over the new government's commitment to the EU pact, which is designed to enforce spending discipline among members of economic and monetary union.

French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin has said he does not feel bound by the pact, which includes stiff fines for governments with excessive deficits, and would seek renegotiation of its stringent terms.
Speaking on Friday from a European Social Democratic Parties Convention in Sweden, Jospin said it was too early to give his government's position on monetary union or a stability pact.
